title: MCI or MCIC?
hook: Could one company's news move an unrelated ticker?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish name similarity from a shared claim on company cash flows.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish name similarity from a shared claim on company cash flows.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In a toy market, telecom value rises 20% from 100. A separate fund at fifty has no claim on its cash flow and no change input. What is the fund’s modeled value? Toy inputs A=[100, 20, 50, 0]; B=[100, 20, 50, 20].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[120, 50, 50], [120, 60, 50]]. Labels: Telecom after, Fund after, Fund before.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The correct mapping leaves the unrelated fund unchanged. The contrast deliberately misroutes the telecom’s change to it. Similar names do not create a shared cash-flow claim in this explicit toy model.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Telecom before=100, Telecom change %=20, Fund before=50, Fund change %=20. What is Fund after? Answer: 60.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Telecom before=100, Telecom change %=20, Fund before=50, Fund change %=20. What is Fund after?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 60. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Shares of a small fund with ticker MCI moved with news about the telecom MCI Communications, whose ticker was MCIC (Rashes, 2001).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish name similarity from a shared claim on company cash flows.
